question: How does BSP scale CET across the Northeast?
html:
Scaling CET across the Northeast

BSP scales CET in three phases: merge MA and CT around Horton, buy founder-owned firms in RI, NH, ME and VT, then add recurring service lines that earn a higher multiple. The target is about 3x revenue in 36 months, following the Smith + Howard path (CET growth plan).

Phase 1: one MA–CT company

  • Horton is the first adjacent-state add-on. It nearly doubles the workforce and brings Connecticut wastewater relationships (CET growth plan).
  • Point Horton at the 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects in CT, MA and RI. New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk lead the list (CET growth plan).
  • Funded CT programs where Horton can prime include Fairfield (about $36.1M across four pump stations and the treatment plant) and Danbury electrical resiliency (about $3.2M) (CET opportunity radar).

Phase 2: adjacent-state add-ons

  • CET already holds licenses in six states. The screen has 48 companies with a median of about $15.1M (CET growth plan).
  • There is a gap. Nine of the top ten ranked targets are in MA and one is in CT. None are in RI, NH, ME or VT (CET add-on targets).
  • Radar coverage is also thin in RI (4 items) and NH (5 items) (CET opportunity radar).
  • Revenue figures are ZoomInfo model estimates and need diligence (CET add-on targets).
  • Competing sponsors, such as Pfingsten's NEC Group and Ridgemont's Crete United, are already active (CET growth plan).

Phase 3: recurring service mix

  • SCADA, pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency work turn one-off bids into contracts (CET growth plan).
  • Advisors price this service mix 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).
  • Data-center work is a thin upside in New England (CET growth plan).

  • These are labelled assumptions, not guidance. The month-0 baselines are low-confidence estimates built from public filings (CET growth plan).
  • The month-36 target assumes about 25% recurring service mix (CET growth plan).

Demand signal

  • September 2026 housing permits: MA 1,515 units, ME 587, NH 459, CT 408, RI 166, VT 152 (Census building permits).
  • These are residential figures. They are a weak proxy for CET's municipal and wastewater work. State revolving-fund priority lists would be a better test of demand by state.

Next actions

  • Fill the target gap. Build a RI, NH, ME and VT target list before Phase 2. Start with the ME and VT radar items, since those states have the most coverage outside MA and CT.

  • Book engineer-of-record meetings. Schedule meetings for the Fairfield, South Windsor, West Haven and Danbury pump-station programs.
  • Pull the MassDEP list by hand. Itemize the 76 projects in the MassDEP 2026 revolving-fund plan. Automated access was blocked (CET opportunity radar).

# Scaling CET across the Northeast

BSP scales CET in three phases: merge MA and CT around Horton, buy founder-owned firms in RI, NH, ME and VT, then add recurring service lines that earn a higher multiple. The target is about 3x revenue in 36 months, following the Smith + Howard path (CET growth plan).

## Phase 1: one MA–CT company

- Horton is the first adjacent-state add-on. It nearly doubles the workforce and brings Connecticut wastewater relationships (CET growth plan).
- Point Horton at the 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects in CT, MA and RI. New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk lead the list (CET growth plan).
- Funded CT programs where Horton can prime include Fairfield (about $36.1M across four pump stations and the treatment plant) and Danbury electrical resiliency (about $3.2M) (CET opportunity radar).

## Phase 2: adjacent-state add-ons

- CET already holds licenses in six states. The screen has 48 companies with a median of about $15.1M (CET growth plan).
- There is a gap. Nine of the top ten ranked targets are in MA and one is in CT. None are in RI, NH, ME or VT (CET add-on targets).
- Radar coverage is also thin in RI (4 items) and NH (5 items) (CET opportunity radar).
- Revenue figures are ZoomInfo model estimates and need diligence (CET add-on targets).
- Competing sponsors, such as Pfingsten's NEC Group and Ridgemont's Crete United, are already active (CET growth plan).

## Phase 3: recurring service mix

- SCADA, pump-station monitoring, solar and storage O&M, EV depot charging and NuWave efficiency work turn one-off bids into contracts (CET growth plan).
- Advisors price this service mix 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).
- Data-center work is a thin upside in New England (CET growth plan).

## KPI roadmap (all est.)

| Month | Revenue | EBITDA | Headcount | Locations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | $80M | $8.0M | 275 | 4 |
| 12 | $115M | $12.1M | 390 | 7 |
| 24 | $170M | $19.5M | 560 | 10 |
| 36 | $240M | $30.0M | 780 | 13 |

- These are labelled assumptions, not guidance. The month-0 baselines are low-confidence estimates built from public filings (CET growth plan).
- The month-36 target assumes about 25% recurring service mix (CET growth plan).

## Demand signal

- September 2026 housing permits: MA 1,515 units, ME 587, NH 459, CT 408, RI 166, VT 152 (Census building permits).
- These are residential figures. They are a weak proxy for CET's municipal and wastewater work. State revolving-fund priority lists would be a better test of demand by state.

## Next actions

- **Fill the target gap.** Build a RI, NH, ME and VT target list before Phase 2. Start with the ME and VT radar items, since those states have the most coverage outside MA and CT.
- **Close the October bid loop.** Log win/loss results for the October bids, including the Massport Worcester airport and the generator jobs. Bid the MassWildlife hatchery generators, which are due Nov 25, 2026.
- **Book engineer-of-record meetings.** Schedule meetings for the Fairfield, South Windsor, West Haven and Danbury pump-station programs.
- **Pull the MassDEP list by hand.** Itemize the 76 projects in the MassDEP 2026 revolving-fund plan. Automated access was blocked (CET opportunity radar).
